ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Consolidated List of Financial Sanctions of Luxembourg and the European Union, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN sanctions lists for USD-denominated transactions, and recognized PEP databases. The screening must be completed prior to incorporation by the notary or a Luxembourg-regulated professional (lawyer or fiduciary), documented in an AML/CFT file under Article 6 of the Law of 12 November 2004, and refreshed periodically pursuant to CSSF Circular L. 12-02 and the Law of 13 January 2019.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must contain the mandatory legal-form suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée'. Names may be expressed in French, German, Luxembourgish, or another Latin-script language; non-Latin characters must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The chosen name must be legally distinguishable from existing trademarks and registered company names, must not mislead the public, and must be acceptable under Luxembourg public policy and moral standards.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Société de crédit / Finance / Fonds (implying regulated financial institution or collective investment vehicle)
État / National / Royal / Municipal (implying state authority)
Chambre / Bourse / Syndicat (subject to professional exclusivity rules)
any word implying a regulated profession or activity for which no license has been obtained
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may request a pre-clearance ('certificat de non-confusion') from the RCS. If the name is rejected, the applicant must obtain the RCS's written grounds of refusal; in such case, the applicant may file a declaratory petition and administrative appeal before the Tribunal Administratif within three (3) months from notification of the rejection. Simultaneously, an alternative name should be submitted through the same RCS online portal to avoid delays. Legal counsels should be engaged for contested names involving IP or prior trademark rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or administrative domiciliation is permissible through an approved Luxembourg domiciliation company. The registered office must be a physical address where legal correspondence can be served and where central administration or accounting records are or can be kept. For an FPV racing drone retail business whose payment rails are PayPal and Stripe, a third-party registered-office arrangement is generally accepted if the service provider is lawfully established in Luxembourg and the company maintains substantive management and operational substance either in Luxembourg or in a manner compliant with tax substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: ≈20% risk of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months by the Luxembourg RCS, tax authorities or economic substance investigators, especially if the registered office is a domiciliation address and the company has unusual or irregular banking patterns.

stage_2.operating_license_title: Official title of operational or manufacturing permit

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; central official portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident investor incorporating a Luxembourg SARL: (1) execute a notarial deed of incorporation; (2) file with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) through the single guichet.lu electronic filing portal to obtain the national identification number (NIF) and RCS matricule; (3) apply to the AEDT for the LU-prefixed 8-digit VAT ID (non-established suppliers must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative for certain supplies); (4) the ACD tax file for corporate income tax and municipal business tax is opened upon registration; no sectoral business licence is required for ISIC 3240 FPV drone manufacturing and retail.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid pass-through election exists; a SARL is a statutorily opaque corporate taxpayer. Applicable elections: VAT grouping (assujetti unique) for related Luxembourg persons; fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) for 99%-owned qualifying subsidiaries; participation exemption election for qualifying dividends and capital gains; and advance tax ruling applications (art. 29a LIR) to the ACD for cross-border structuring certainty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (VAT Law of 12 February 1979)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT) below which the small-enterprise exemption (franchise en base) applies; mandatory VAT registration once this threshold is exceeded, when intra-Community distance sales surpass EUR 10,000, or when OSS/IOSS is used for cross-border e-commerce sales of racing drones.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping for ordinary B2B/B2C supplies; B2G suppliers must issue e-invoices via the national PEPPOL access point for public-sector contracts; private traders may mutually agree EDI or structured e-invoice formats, and all invoices and export evidence must be archived for at least 10 years for AEDT/ACD audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU where the supplier has transferred the power of disposal to the customer and proves the goods' EU exit within the statutory time limit (art. 51 VAT Law); 0% also applies to identified offshore supplies of drone assembly, repair, calibration, and technical services under art. 58 VAT Law where the recipient is an entrepreneur established outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic declaration with Movement Reference Number - MRN from Luxembourg customs)
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill or air waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU territory
Commercial invoice / pro-forma invoice / purchase order setting out goods description, quantity, and buyer details
Bank credit advice or Inward Remittance Certificate confirming receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT and customs audits scrutinise export zero-rating files, normally within the five-year VAT assessment limitation period; unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating is recharacterised as a domestic taxable supply, triggering immediate VAT clawback, default interest at 0.8% per month, penal surcharges of up to 10% (which may reach 100% in bad-faith cases), criminal fraude fiscale fines of up to EUR 25,000 and custodial penalties for responsible managers, and suspension or forfeiture of rights to VAT refund under the 13th Directive procedures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem framework of the European Central Bank (ECB). Prudential supervision of Luxembourg credit institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). The BCL is responsible for monetary policy operations, TARGET2 participation, payment-system oversight, foreign-exchange statistics and balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting, while the CSSF applies EU banking, AML/CFT and markets rules to all licensed banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility. As a euro-area Member State, Luxembourg applies the EU Treaty framework of free movement of capital and payments under Article 63 TFEU, and there are no exchange-control authorisations, licensing requirements or surrender obligations for current-account or capital-account flows. Profit remittance is unrestricted at FX level, but a distribution requires ordinary shareholders' approval, availability of distributable reserves verified against Luxembourg statutory accounts, and compliance with withholding taxes: the domestic rate on dividends is 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and the domestic participation-exemption conditions (qualifying holding of at least 10% held for at least 12 months, effective-substance and anti-abuse tests under article 166 LIR), and further reduced under applicable double tax treaties. The entity must also satisfy BCL BOP statistical reporting, CSSF AML/KYC documentation, and Luxembourg FDI screening under Regulation (EU) 2023/1734 for non-EU direct investors where applicable. No central-bank clearance for incoming or outgoing payments is required in normal euro payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio into EUR, and no timing deadline for repatriation of export receivables (statutory conversion ratio is 0% and the retention period is unrestricted). Export receipts may be held indefinitely in USD, CNH, EUR or other foreign currency in a segregated corporate FX account. The only compliance overlays are: (i) BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting for cross-border flows and positions above the BCL survey materiality thresholds under BPM6 methodology; (ii) CSSF AML/CFT obligations to maintain underlying trade documents, invoices, airway bills and shipping evidence supporting each FX conversion or international settlement; and (iii) Luxembourg VAT rules for intra-EU and export supplies of drones, including periodic recapitulative statements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Blocked Account (Compte bloqué) for SARL share-capital deposit; Operational Current Account with segregated EUR and FX sub-ledgers
Capital Escrow Blocked Account and Operating Current Account; incremental trade-finance facilities (documentary letters of credit, foreign supplier guarantees, FX forward lines)
Capital Escrow Blocked Account; Operating Current Account with SEPA Credit Transfer, SEPA Instant and PayPal/Stripe payout crediting
Operating Current Account with global transaction-banking package, USD clearing via foreign nostro network and dedicated FX desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions exercising PSD2 passporting rights into Luxembourg. PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. et Cie, S.C.A. holds a CSSF e-money licence and is the natural primary PSP for the EU and cross-border FPV drone retail rails; Stripe Technology Europe DAC (Ireland) passports payment services into Luxembourg and settles via SEPA payouts to a tier-1 Luxembourg bank account. Medium for United Kingdom-based APMs and fintechs: post-Brexit EU passporting has ceased, so a UK EMI requires either a Luxembourg branch authorisation, an EU-licensed partner bank, or reliance on the FCA temporary-permissions regime for inbound cross-border services, which banks only partially accept. Low and generally Prohibited for non-EEA offshore digital EMIs: offering payment accounts, acquiring, or virtual-IBAN 'rent-a-rail' services to Luxembourg residents without CSSF or ECB authorisation is a criminal offence under the Luxembourg law of 10 August 2020 on payment services (transposing PSD2); commercial banks will refuse to credit an unwrapped offshore EMI float.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is effectively mandatory for initial onboarding. BCEE, BGL BNP Paribas and BIL require at least one managing director and the individual Ultimate Beneficial Owner(s) to attend a face-to-face KYC interview at the Luxembourg branch with original passports, proof of residential address and corporate documentation. Fully remote onboarding is not available for newly incorporated non-resident SARLs: videoconference KYC may supplement, but does not replace, physical verification, while executed powers of attorney must be notarised and apostilled under the Hague Convention of 1961. Under the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004 as amended by the law of 25 March 2020 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, the bank must positively identify the client, identify and verify every UBO (more than 25% ownership) and establish the source of funds before any transaction. Realistic timeline for full onboarding is two to four weeks after submission of a complete original dossier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity opacity: bank account sought by a newly incorporated Luxembourg SARL whose shareholders and UBOs are tax-resident outside the EU/EEA, with no domestic physical substance at the registered office.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation; RCS excerpt (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés); LEI certificate; articles of association with Luxembourg registered office; Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) filing proof; apostilled powers of attorney; notarised UBO self-certification and source-of-wealth form; tax residence certificates of all shareholders; source-of-funds bank reference for the capital injection; business plan and 12-month cash-flow forecast; lease contract for Luxembourg premises; payroll and social-security filings for resident staff.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use export-control exposure: FPV drones and components may fall under Annex I of EU Dual-Use Regulation (EU) 2021/821 if endurance, camera resolution, autonomous-flight or payload parameters exceed control thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written export-control classification certificate prepared by qualified counsel or an accredited EU dual-use consultant; technical datasheets proving endurance, speed, camera, and payload remain below Annex I thresholds; OEM supplier declarations for carbon-fibre frames, motors, flight controllers and batteries; end-use certificates from distributors; documented internal export-compliance manual; sanctions screening log; TARIC commodity codes and customs tariff classifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume e-commerce micro-settlement pattern: PayPal/Stripe payout aggregation with recurring chargebacks and rapid onward transfers, which banks may construe as structuring or mule-account behaviour.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Acquirer settlement reports (PayPal and Stripe) cross-matched line-by-line with SEPA bank credits; ERP order and inventory report (Shopify, WooCommerce or Odoo) evidencing physical sales of racing drones; logistics tracking evidence (DPD, UPS, e-packets); Luxembourg VAT returns filed with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA; refund and chargeback logs; PSD2 dispute correspondence; annual financial statements reconciling e-commerce revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and prohibited-jurisdiction leakage: sales of FPV drones to embargoed territories, sanctioned entities, or diversion-risk buyers detected on payment rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geoblocking configuration (IP, shipping address and bank-account blocks) aligned with EU consolidated sanctions and OFAC; real-time KYB/KYC buyer screening on PayPal/Stripe checkout; World-Check or RiskScreen negative-news screening reports; jurisdiction restriction clauses in e-commerce terms of sale; Internal Compliance Programme approved by the board; blocked-transaction and freezing logs; sanctions attestation signed by the managing director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Profit tunnel, thin capitalisation and substance mismatch: interim dividends or shareholder-loan repayments proposed while the SARL is early-stage and managed from abroad.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders' meeting minutes authorising the distribution; statutory auditor report or approved statutory auditor certificate on distributable reserves; audited or approved annual accounts demonstrating positive net assets; arm's-length interest rate on shareholder loans evidenced by loan agreement and OECD transfer-pricing documentation; Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net-wealth tax filings; payroll, social security and substance records for the Luxembourg office.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholders wire the subscribed SARL share capital (minimum EUR 12,000; at least 25% of each cash share paid up at constitution; in-kind contributions fully transferred) into a blocked attestation account in the name of the société en formation at BCEE, BGL BNP Paribas or BIL. The bank runs sanctions, UBO and source-of-funds KYC, then issues an attestation de blocage, which the notary files with the RCS on incorporation. After registration the blocked funds are released to the operating account. For inbound shareholder loans and group cash, use SWIFT MT103/TARGET2 in EUR or the relevant nostro chain for USD/CNH, quoting ISO 20022 purpose code CAPG for capital injection or INTC for intra-company treasury; the BCL BOP declaration must classify equity and loan injections separately, and arm's-length interest documentation is required to avoid recharacterisation. All customer wires must quote the purpose, the underlying contract, and the beneficiary LEI to satisfy CSSF AML and BCL statistical rules. No central-bank FX approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails available to the Luxembourg SARL: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pacs.008) and SEPA Instant (pacs.009) for euro settlements with EU suppliers of carbon-fibre frames, motors, ESCs and batteries; (2) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers in USD, CNH or JPY via BGL BNP Paribas and Société Générale Luxembourg nostro relationships, settled over Fedwire/CHIPS for USD and CNAPS/HSBC clearing for CNH; (3) commercial letters of credit issued under ICC UCP 600 for import and export consignments, with documentary presentations checked by the Luxembourg issuing bank and SWIFT MT700/MT754/MT710 messaging; (4) documentary collections under ICC URC 522; (5) e-commerce merchant payout rails: PayPal (Europe) and Stripe settle as aggregated SEPA Credit Transfers to the SARL's bank account, referencing order settlement reports. Every outgoing disbursement must quote the underlying invoice, commercial contract or LC reference to satisfy CSSF AML transaction monitoring, BCL balance-of-payments reporting, and Luxembourg VAT invoicing rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot Transactions (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH) settled through the corporate bank's dealing desk or CLS-eligible channels
FX Outright Forwards (up to 12 months) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or bank's standard FX Master Terms governed by Luxembourg law
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in currencies with restricted deliverability (e.g., offshore CNH reference or INR-leg structures where physical settlement is unavailable)
Cross-Currency Swaps (XCCY, typically EUR/USD) to hedge long-term intercompany funding and trade payables
European-Style Currency Options (EUR/USD, bought or sold premium) for risk management of uncertain future receipts

All OTC derivatives are subject to EMIR (Regulation (EU) 648/2012 as amended by EMIR Refit (EU) 2019/834) trade reporting to registered trade repositories, uncleared-margin rules where applicable, and KYC documentation under a Luxembourg-law ISDA or collateral agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year end; for calendar-year accounts, standard deadline is 30 September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 10,000 per late filing; court order may compel filing; three consecutive years of default trigger administrative dissolution/strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation (Confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs) – RBE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 December of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 20,000 for the company and up to EUR 5,000 per director; imprisonment (8 days to 6 months) for repeated non-compliance; administrative strike-off in extreme cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if any two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average number of employees > 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002, as amended); IFRS permitted for certain entities and consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All UBO changes, including shareholding transfers, must be reported to the RBE within 30 days. An annual confirmation validating the accuracy of RBE data must be completed by 31 December each year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined rate for 2024: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.86% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime: 80% exemption on qualifying IP income (effective rate 4.94%); participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (100% exempt subject to 10% minimum interest and 12-month holding); notional interest deduction (NID) limited to the excess of new equity over the previous tax year; investment tax credits for qualifying digital and ecological assets; effective rate for industrial/factory activities may be reduced through accelerated depreciation on carbon-fiber milling equipment and robotics.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (subject to Article 114 LIR conditions; anti-abuse restrictions on change of beneficial ownership and change of business activity)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Déclaration collective pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune) – filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu (eCDF portal) using the Luxembourg SEDLL/FTAM system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; extension possible to 31 March and then to 30 June upon request. For a fiscal year ending 31 December 2024, the filing deadline is 31 December 2025 unless an extension is granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg tax ID (matricule), registered address, principal industrial activity (ISIC 3240; FPV racing drone manufacturing).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident SARL operating through a Luxembourg branch or permanent establishment, use the branch's Luxembourg address and quote the branch registration number. Indicate the foreign head office and its tax residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year covered: opening date, closing date, duration in months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the PE's accounting period, mirroring the foreign head office's accounts if the PE is integrated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit/loss per Luxembourg GAAP (loss before tax, as presented in the P&L).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the PE's separate financial statements, or an apportioned profit derived from the foreign head office's accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and add-backs: 50% of meal and entertainment expenses, non-deductible fines, tax penalties, payments to non-tax-transparent offshore jurisdictions without substance, excessive director remuneration or disbursements treated as hidden distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add-back attributable to PE activity only. Non-resident directors' fees are deductible if paid in accordance with arm's length provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation adjustments: ordinary tax depreciation (typically 20%-30% straight-line for machinery; intellectual property software 33.33% straight-line), recapture of excess book depreciation, and any previous extraordinary write-downs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Luxembourg depreciation rates to PE-acquired or PE-assigned assets only. Assets located in Luxembourg are depreciated per Luxembourg tables regardless of foreign head-office treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward: available off-setting losses from prior years (unlimited carryforward under the continuity test).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses economically attributable to the Luxembourg PE may be deducted. Foreign head-office losses are not automatically transferable unless a Luxembourg treaty or entry level facility applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before tax credits: result of Box 3 adjusted by Boxes 4–6, and after applying participation exemption, IP box exemption and notional interest deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must exclude non-Luxembourg-source income. Apply Luxembourg-specific positive adjustments to arrive at the local branch taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IP regime deduction (80% of net qualifying IP income, including licensing and embedded royalties on FPV drone software/design patents).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available only if the qualifying IP was developed or is economically owned by the Luxembourg PE and the income is attributable to the PE. Separate documentation required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Notional interest deduction (NID): calculated on the increase of qualifying equity contributed after 17 June 2021, rate capped at 30% of the excess of new equity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not available to a PE unless the foreign head office assigns capital to the PE and the NID election is disclosed. Subject to substance and anti-abuse review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and the calculation of corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), solidarity surcharge, and net wealth tax (BEF/IF), including foreign tax credit relief for taxes paid abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credit only for income attributable to the PE which is also taxed abroad. Attach Form 500A (foreign tax credit declaration).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 'tax increase' of 10% of the assessed tax, subject to a cap of EUR 12,500; late-payment interest at 0.6% per month on the unpaid amount; administrative fines from the AGD up to EUR 5,000 for each omitted declaration; in case of income tax evasion, a criminal fine up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of up to five years. The taxpayer may also be subject to an official assessment based on deemed facts, with the burden of proof shifted to the taxpayer.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on distributions to corporate and individual shareholders; reduced to 0% for a qualifying parent company under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (SAARL acting as a direct parent, ≥10% shareholding and holding period of at least 12 months), and for Luxembourg resident parent companies meeting the 10%/12-month participation exemption; treaty-provisioned rates frequently 5% or 10% (e.g., US: 5% with ≥10% holding; UK: 0% with ≥10% holding).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty withholding rate, the beneficiary must file Form 720 (Demande de remboursement/liquidation) with the Luxembourg Administration des Contributions Directes together with (i) the official tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, (ii) a sworn statement of beneficial ownership, (iii) proof of shareholding and holding period, and (iv)—if applicable—approval from the Luxembourg direct tax administration (bureau d'imposition). The reduced rate may be applied at source only after the paying agent obtains a prior issuance of the 'autorisation de liquidation' from the AGD; otherwise the full 15% is withheld and a refund claim must be filed within the statute of limitations (generally by 31 December of the third year after the distribution).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Luxembourg statutory withholding tax on outbound royalty payments (no domestic WHT on licensing income derived from patents, copyrights, know-how or software); interest: 0% statutory withholding tax on most outbound interest payments (loans, bonds, advances), with minor exception for profit-participating loans which may be recharacterized as dividends. Treaty provisions may reduce or eliminate any residual charge; however, the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive and the Interest & Royalty Directive require beneficial ownership and genuine substance to maintain a 0% rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 100,000 for intercompany service transactions; EUR 500,000 for inventory, goods, royalties and financial transactions; master file/CbCR obligatory for MNE groups with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750,000,000. The Luxembourg tax administration (AGD) may require lower thresholds upon request under Circular LIR 56/1-56/20.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to UAE/Caribbean jurisdictions; however, the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR), the EU ATAD, beneficial ownership tests, and the jurisprudence on 'artificial arrangements' impose an effective substance requirement. A SARL manufacturing and distributing FPV racing drones must demonstrate management presence in Luxembourg, physical premises (or leased facilities), personnel (engineering, production, sales staff) and actual risk control for supply-chain functions. Without such substance, the tax administration may deny treaty benefits, participation exemption, parent-subsidiary WHT exemption and may recharacterize the structure as a shell company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting taxable income from the Form 500 filing, falsifying books or records, creating backdated invoices, or misrepresenting the actual number of FPV drone units sold to avoid taxable income in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fractional reassessment preserving a 10-year statute of limitations; tax increase of 50% of the evaded tax; late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; criminal fine of EUR 25,000; imprisonment of up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers and shadow directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate taxes if the evasion was committed with their knowledge or negligence. Civil recovery may attach to personal assets; criminal proceedings may trigger travel bans, provisional detention and, on conviction, a prison sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering a Luxembourg SARL used solely as a conduit for invoicing FPV drone sales without any physical presence, local employees, decision-making power, or central administration in Luxembourg; hiding capital through a third-party nominee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 6 LIR (abuse of law), the tax authorities may ignore the corporate veil for tax purposes, deny treaty relief, reject the participation exemption, reclassify the income as derived by the ultimate shareholder, and re-open the assessment period up to 10 years. Additional penalties equal to 100% of the tax avoided may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers are personally liable for the amounts of tax, interest, and penalties not collected from the corporate vehicle. A travel ban and freezing of personal assets may be imposed during investigation; wrongful trading constitutes a criminal offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing carbon-fiber material purchases from an Asian related affiliate, overpaying for IP licenses to a foreign group company, or not documenting the arm's-length margin of the drone distribution activity; failing to prepare adequate local-file/master-file documentation within the statutory production period (30 days after AGD request).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment to the Luxembourg taxable income; secondary adjustment (recharacterization of hidden distribution); late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; administrative penalty of up to 20% of the resulting under-assessment; in severe cases, a penalty equal to the excess income-shifting amount plus interest. The unlawful deduction is disallowed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign or approve non-arm's-length transfer prices are jointly liable for the additional tax and interest. If the misstatement involves false evidence or tax fraud, criminal liability of the director may lead to imprisonment and personal seizure of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) in the Luxembourg Registry of Beneficial Owners (RBE), refusing to disclose the identity of actual shareholders in the SARL, or permitting the use of the drone sales revenue to receive crypto or fiat payments from sanctioned jurisdictions without conducting adequate KYC/CDD procedures (even if the risk-tier is 'Low_Risk_Standard').
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019 (AML register), administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 or 1% of annual turnover; separate criminal fine up to EUR 1 million for serious breaches. The director may be banned from serving as manager or director for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for AML failures if they acted with intent or gross negligence; personal asset freezing, travel bans, and civil restitution to investors or creditors (including tax creditors) are applicable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late or Non-filing of Corporation Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the statutory deadline for Form 500 (or failing to pay estimated instalments) beyond a three-month grace period after the AGD request, or refusing to file the annual return altogether.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic assessment based on the AGD's estimation; late-filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax (capped at EUR 12,500); late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; additional fine of EUR 50 per day of continued non-compliance, not exceeding EUR 5,000; cancellation of the tax clearance certificate necessary for public markets and borrowing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who remain non-compliant can be held jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt, subject to a 5-year ban on managing any Luxembourg entity. Persistent non-filing may escalate to criminal prosecution for fraud.
